layers.note: An introduced herb of clearings, logged ground, burns and forest edges.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −5 °C, gone by −10 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Lows to about −26 °C borne, gone below about −34 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warmest-month means from about 13 to 25 °C, gone below 10 °C and above 29 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 2,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 900 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 500.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.55, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; naturalised under summer-dry and summer-wet temperate climates to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Foxglove, from western Europe, is naturalised in clearings of the Pacific Northwest's humid forests (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
